title: Infection Prevention and Control
subtitle: For staff at Pennsylvania personal care homes and assisted living facilities. 55 Pa. Code 2600.65(f)(4) and 2800.65(i)(4), which pair infection control with the risks of immobility.

title: How an infection actually gets from one resident to the next

eyebrow: Break any one link and it stops
title: The route almost every spread takes
points: Hands — the single busiest vehicle in the building
Shared equipment moving room to room
High-touch surfaces: rails, bells, knobs, handles
Droplets from a cough at conversational distance
Soiled linen, waste, and anything shaken out

title: Hand hygiene, done the way it actually works
When hands get cleaned, every time
points: Before you touch a resident, and after
Before anything clean: dressings, meals, meds
After body fluids, always
After gloves come off — not instead of
After touching the room, resident or not

title: The spots hands miss on their own
points: Thumbs — the most skipped surface on the hand
Fingertips and under the nails
Between the fingers
The wrists, if a cuff or a glove sat there
Rings, watches, and long nails hold what you just washed off

eyebrow: The exception people carry down the hall
quote: Alcohol does not kill C. diff spores. It moves them.
attribution: Diarrhea of any cause means soap, water, friction, and a rinse. The pump on the wall is the wrong tool, and it feels exactly like the right one.

title: Personal protective equipment, and the sixty seconds it fails in

eyebrow: On in this order, off in reverse
title: Putting it on, taking it off
points: On: hands, gown, mask, eyewear, gloves
Off: gloves, eyewear, gown, then mask
Gloves first — the dirtiest thing on you
Mask last, outside the room, by the ties
Clean hands after gloves, and at the end

eyebrow: Every one of these is common
title: How protective equipment stops protecting
points: A mask under the nose, or pulled to talk
Gloves worn room to room to save a trip
A phone or a door opened with gloves on
A gown pulled off over the head
Adjusting a mask with the gloves you wore

title: Surfaces, equipment, and the two-second wipe

eyebrow: The number on the label is the product
quote: If it dries in twenty seconds and the label says two minutes, you cleaned it. You did not disinfect it.
attribution: The surface has to stay visibly wet for the whole contact time. Everything else on that bottle is packaging.

eyebrow: Between residents — not end of shift
title: Equipment that travels, and what it carries
points: Blood pressure cuff, thermometer, glucose meter
Wheelchairs, walkers, the lift and its sling
Bed rails, call bells, over-bed tables
Doorknobs, handrails, light switches
Anything you carried in and will carry back out

quote: You cannot look at a person and know.
attribution: So everybody gets the same protection. The moment you start deciding who seems risky, you get residents judged for a diagnosis that is nobody's business — and the one nobody suspected is the one who spreads it.

title: When precautions go up on a door

eyebrow: What the sign is asking you for
title: Three kinds of added precaution
points: Contact — gown, gloves, dedicated equipment
Droplet — a mask; a cough carries a few feet
Airborne — fitted respirator, door closed
Supplies stocked at the door, in advance
Read the sign every time — it changes

eyebrow: The part the sign does not say
quote: A precaution sign is about an organism. It is not a verdict on a person.
attribution: Residents on precautions get visited less, talked to less, and touched less, and they feel every bit of it. Suit up, then go in and stay a while.

title: Noticing early, and saying it out loud

eyebrow: Two is a pattern, not a coincidence
title: What a cluster looks like before anyone calls it one
points: Two residents, same hall, same symptom
Staff calling off with the same thing
Several trays coming back untouched
A rash, or diarrhea, in more than one room
Say it the day you notice it

title: What stops when a resident stops moving
points: Muscle is lost in days, not months
Skin breaks down over hips and tailbone
Lungs stop clearing — pneumonia gets in
Everything backs up, appetite included
Turning and walking are infection control

eyebrow: What to carry out of this course
quote: Do this well and you prevent illnesses nobody will ever know about, including your own.
attribution: There is no thank you for those. That is the job.
